title: Build Applications on NVIDIA BlueField Faster with NVIDIA DOCA Agent Skills | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA released DOCA agent skills (SKILL.md files with verified APIs, hardware capabilities and build constraints) and reports that on 65 DOCA prompts agents scored 19% of checklist items without them and 100% with them. A BlueField-3 RDMA demo showed 73% less handwritten code with skills.

insights.claim: In NVIDIA's 65-prompt DOCA evaluation, general-purpose AI agents without domain skills satisfied only 19% of graded checklist items, versus 100% across all 65 prompts with DOCA skills.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Vendor-run benchmark; shows how large the domain-knowledge gap is for general agents on specialized infrastructure software.
insights.locator: Why do AI agents need a foundation for DOCA development?

insights.claim: Without skills, agents misused DOCA APIs and flags in 59 of 65 prompts, failed to verify hardware capability in 46, mis-routed tools in 39, skipped smoke tests in 34 and guessed versions in 30.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Quantifies where generic coding agents break on hardware-specific stacks: invented APIs and unverified hardware assumptions.
insights.locator: Without the skills, agents consistently made the same mistakes

insights.claim: General-purpose agents pattern-match from broad training data rather than verified DOCA API contracts, because the DOCA library surface is large, fast-evolving and hardware-specific, with no machine-readable contract to reason from.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Explains why niche infrastructure SDKs need curated agent context; a moat for vendors that ship skills.
insights.locator: When you ask a general-purpose AI agent to set up a DOCA Comch

insights.claim: Agents inventing nonexistent functions, flags and image tags was the most frequent failure, forcing developers to debug errors they did not introduce.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Hallucinated APIs are a hidden productivity tax in infrastructure development.

insights.claim: DOCA AI agent skills are an open, lightweight format built around a SKILL.md file containing real API signatures, hardware capability requirements and build constraints, scoped per DOCA component such as Flow, GPUNetIO, PCC and RDMA.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is packaging its software stack as agent-consumable skills, extending its ecosystem lock-in into AI-assisted development.
insights.locator: What are DOCA AI agent skills?

insights.claim: A DOCA skill is positioned as a machine-readable specification the agent reasons against directly, not just a summary of documentation, and it does not replace the agent.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Signals a shift from human-readable docs to agent-readable contracts as a distribution channel for developer platforms.
insights.quote: The skills are not just a summary of documentation, but a machine-readable specification the agent can reason against directly.
insights.locator: What are DOCA AI agent skills?

insights.claim: DOCA is positioned as the unified software platform for NVIDIA BlueField DPUs, spanning accelerated networking, AI-native storage, in-silicon security, telemetry and lifecycle management for agentic AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Shows NVIDIA's framing of BlueField as core AI infrastructure; developer tooling investment supports DPU adoption.
insights.locator: DOCA is the unified software platform

insights.claim: Skills make agents verify device support, such as GPU-NIC PCIe topology and GPUNetIO availability, before writing code, instead of discovering mismatches on real hardware.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Pre-code hardware validation reduces rework cycles in GPU-direct networking projects.
insights.locator: Verify hardware before writing any code

insights.claim: In firmware-level change scenarios on a live BlueField-3 DPU, the with-skills agent met every requirement (preflight inventory, out-of-band path, maintenance window, rollback plan, cold power-cycle awareness) while the without-skills agent met none.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: The largest gap appeared in the highest-risk tasks, which is where agent reliability matters most for production infrastructure.
insights.locator: Execute changes that affect hardware safely

insights.claim: mlxconfig-class firmware writes on BlueField take effect only after a cold power cycle, not a warm reboot, which generic agents did not account for.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Operational detail relevant to DPU fleet management and maintenance planning.
insights.locator: Execute changes that affect hardware safely

insights.claim: Build-correctness was tested on only 10 of 65 prompts, but failures there block progress entirely; the skill-equipped agent correctly used pkg-config to resolve a doca_flow_init link error.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Narrow sample, but illustrates build-system knowledge as part of the skill value.
insights.locator: Ship code that compiles and links

insights.claim: In a side-by-side demo building a Go-based RDMA application on BlueField-3, the with-skills agent used 73% less handwritten code (189 versus 695 lines) and 46% fewer hardware commands (20 versus 37); both agents succeeded.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Concrete efficiency claim; the benefit is fewer correction cycles rather than task success, so value is in iteration cost.

insights.claim: NVIDIA argues the reduction in correction cycles compounds across every developer, task and deployment for teams using AI agents on DOCA at scale.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Marketing framing, but supports a thesis that agent-ready tooling lowers the cost of building on NVIDIA networking silicon.
insights.locator: What are the benefits of DOCA agent skills for developers?

insights.claim: The skills are published openly in the NVIDIA/skills GitHub repository, with general skills plus library-specific ones for DOCA Flow, GPUNetIO and RDMA.
insights.speaker: Claudia Martinez
insights.so_what: Watch adoption of NVIDIA/skills as a signal of how NVIDIA extends its software moat to agentic development.
insights.locator: Get started with NVIDIA DOCA AI agent skills
